text.en: You eat a roti at lunch. By evening it is gone, but it has become energy and part of your body. How? Animals use food through digestion, breathing, circulation and excretion.

Animals cannot make their own food. They get nutrients by eating plants or other animals. Digestion is breaking food into small simple substances the body can absorb. In humans it starts in the mouth, where teeth chew and saliva begins digesting starch. Food passes through the food pipe to the stomach, where acids and juices work, then to the small intestine, where most digestion and absorption happen. The large intestine takes in water and the rest leaves as waste.
In aerobic respiration, cells use oxygen to release energy from food. Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide and less oxygen than inhaled air. The lungs exchange gases. Fish use gills and insects use tiny tubes.
The heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of the body. Blood carries food and oxygen to cells and takes away waste. Red blood cells carry oxygen. Plasma carries food. White blood cells fight germs.
Excretion is removing waste from the body. The kidneys filter blood and make urine. Lungs remove carbon dioxide and the skin removes sweat.
Animals cannot make their own food. They get nutrients by eating plants or other animals.
Digestion is breaking food into small simple substances the body can absorb. In humans it starts in the mouth, where teeth chew and saliva begins digesting starch.

Food passes through the food pipe to the stomach, where acids and juices work, then to the small intestine, where most digestion and absorption happen. The large intestine takes in water and the rest leaves as waste.
In aerobic respiration, cells use oxygen to release energy from food and produce carbon dioxide. Breathing helps bring in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
The lungs exchange gases. Fish use gills and insects use tiny tubes.
The heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of the body. Blood carries food and oxygen to cells and takes away waste.
Red blood cells carry oxygen. Plasma carries food. White blood cells fight germs.
Excretion is removing waste from the body. The kidneys filter blood and make urine. Lungs remove carbon dioxide and the skin removes sweat.
A bite of banana enters the mouth. Taking food into the body is called ingestion. The next stages prepare its nutrients for absorption.
Teeth break food into smaller pieces. This gives digestive juices more surface to act on.
Saliva moistens food and starts breaking down starch. This shows that digestion begins before a bite reaches the stomach.
After swallowing, muscles in the food pipe move food towards the stomach. Food can travel through the tube even against gravity.
The stomach wall churns food and mixes it with digestive juices. This produces a softer mixture that moves on.
The mixture enters the small intestine. Bile helps break large fat droplets into tiny ones, and digestive juices break down nutrients.
Digestion breaks larger substances into smaller ones. Absorption moves those smaller substances through the intestinal wall into the body.
Some water remains with the undigested material. The large intestine absorbs some of that water before the residue leaves the body.
A cow quickly swallows grass. It later brings partly processed grass back to the mouth and chews it again. That material is called cud.

board.text: A cow swallows grass, then chews cud

text.en: People chew before swallowing and do not bring food back up to chew it again as part of digestion. A cow’s stomach system helps it use a grass diet.
When the chest space gets larger, air moves into the lungs. When the chest space becomes smaller, air moves out.
Tiny air sacs in the lungs sit next to tiny blood vessels. Oxygen moves into the blood and carbon dioxide moves into the air sacs.
Your lungs take up some of the oxygen you breathe in. The air you breathe out still contains oxygen, along with more carbon dioxide than before.
Breathing takes oxygen into the lungs. Blood carries it to cells. In aerobic respiration the cells use oxygen to release usable energy from nutrients.
A fish moves water past its gills. Oxygen dissolved in the water moves into the blood, while carbon dioxide can move into the water.
Air enters an insect through openings on its body and travels through branching tubes. Oxygen can reach tissues through these tubes.
An adult frog uses lungs on land. Gases can also cross its moist skin, a useful route in water.

board.text: Frogs have more than one route

text.en: Blood picks up oxygen near the lungs and delivers it to tissues. The same circulation returns carbon dioxide from tissues to the lungs.
Working muscles need more energy during exercise. Breathing and heart rate usually rise to supply oxygen and carry carbon dioxide away.
Count a full rise and fall of your chest as one breath. Compare the same time intervals at rest and after comfortable movement.
Kidneys remove wastes produced inside the body and make urine. Egestion removes material that passed through the gut without being digested.
Trace starch digestion to absorbable sugars, and trace oxygen from the air sacs to cells. The two routes meet when an actively respiring cell uses them.

board.text: From food and air to energy

problem.en: Where does most digestion and absorption take place?

text.en: Food leaves the stomach.
It enters the small intestine where most digestion and absorption occur.

problem.en: Why is it useful for food to be chewed before it reaches the stomach?

text.en: Teeth break larger pieces into smaller ones.

why.en: More surface is exposed to digestive juices.

text.en: Saliva mixes with the pieces and starts starch digestion.

why.en: Both mechanical breakdown and chemical digestion begin in the mouth.

problem.en: A fish lives underwater. How does it get oxygen without taking in air at the surface?

text.en: Water containing dissolved oxygen passes over the gills.

why.en: The oxygen is present in the water itself.

text.en: Oxygen crosses the gill surface into the blood.

why.en: The fish circulates it to its tissues.

prompt.en: Explain how food reaches every cell of the body.

points.en: Aerobic respiration releases energy in cells using oxygen.
